name: Elisha
overview: Elisha was a male prophet anointed to succeed Elijah, as described in 1 Kings 19:16. He is recognized primarily for carrying forward Elijah's prophetic ministry with divine authority. No specific tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are recorded in the provided information.
namesAndTitles: The name Elisha means 'G-d is my salvation,' highlighting his role as a servant of the true God. He was also known by the title 'man of God,' emphasizing his prophetic office and close relationship with the Lord, as noted in 2 Kings 4:7 and Luke 4:27.
familyAndRelationships: Elisha was the son of Shaphat, as explicitly mentioned in 1 Kings 19:16. He also served as master to Gehazi, indicating a mentor-disciple relationship found in 2 Kings 4:12. Beyond these, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Elisha's significance in Scripture stems from his role as Elijah's prophetic successor, empowered with a double portion of Elijah's spirit. His ministry, which lasted over fifty years, was marked by numerous miracles demonstrating God's power and compassion, such as healing, provision, and raising the dead. These acts prefigure the mercy and authority ultimately fulfilled in Christ's ministry.

keyEvents.event: Received double portion of Elijah's spirit
